abstract.value: Discrete denoising diffusion models (DDMs) have recently emerged as a compelling alternative to autoregressive (AR) modeling for discrete data, offering parallel generation and iterative global refinement capabilities. Unlike continuous diffusion, where the state space is fixed, DDMs are fundamentally shaped by how the discrete state space is constructed: the tokenization scheme, the vocabulary topology, and domain-specific structural alphabets. This work introduces a unified conceptual framework that views discrete diffusion models through the construction of the underlying discrete state space. Within this framework, existing formulations, including transition-matrix, masking/absorbing-state, and score/ratio-based approaches, emerge as different instantiations of a common design space. The framework further exposes common design trade-offs across training objectives, inference algorithms, scaling behavior, systems optimization, and evaluation protocols, suggesting several promising directions for future research.

title.value: Discrete Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework from Tokenization to Generation

abstract.value: Synthesizing reinforcement learning policies using Deep Q learning for continuous-space systems is one of the common goals in robotic applications. But using DQN based policies lack formal guarantees on convergence to optimal policy. One can use tabular Q-learning methods which has optimal policy convergence guarantees.  However, directly transferring tabular Q-learning policies to continuous environments introduces a severe sim-to-real dynamic mismatch, frequently resulting in catastrophic specification violations. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that formally bounds spatial drift without requiring hyper-conservative grid resolutions. A high-level Q-learning agent synthesizes an optimal policy on a highly tractable discrete state-space, while a low-level robust tracking controller forces the continuous physical plant to adhere to the discrete trajectory within a strict $\epsilon$-tube. By actively suppressing this sim-to-real divergence, we mathematically guarantee that the transferred continuous execution strictly satisfies the original temporal and stability specifications, while maintaining a formally bounded $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$ optimality loss relative to the ideal discrete Q-value. The efficacy of the proposed framework is demonstrated through experiments on three nonlinear robotic environments: an omnibot, a 2-DOF helicopter, and an inverted pendulum. Videos of the experiments are available at \href{https://tinyurl.com/2e5c89be}{link}\footnote{https://tinyurl.com/2e5c89be}.

title.value: Formally Guaranteed Policy Transfer for Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Spaces
